title: Conversational fallback sandbox postmortem - action closure
summary: Postmortem and closure session after a production conversational fallback loop in HelioMedix staging that leaked into a small window of production traffic. Goal: review root cause (cache warming + routing fallback mismatch), confirm mitigations, assign owners and schedule a sandbox failover runbook validation in staging with Redwood engineers.
topics: KV cache warming and prefix cache miss
Data privacy and KMS audit notes
Timeline for pilot and Demo of revised fallback logic
action_items: Aisha: Share sanitized request/response samples + filtered logs from the incident (S3 link) - due 2026-03-06
Diego: Deploy fallback patch to staging & run automated canary (48hr) with HelioMedix prompt corpus - due 2026-03-10
Samir: Provide anonymized prompt set and peak traffic profile (CSV) - due 2026-03-06
Maya: Kick off SOC 2 addendum check with HelioMedix security (confirm KMS rotation policy) - due 2026-03-09
Tom: Review and sign redwood DPA addendum draft and send redlines - due 2026-03-11
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour sandbox failover rehearsal week of 2026-03-09
Redwood to enable enhanced tracing on model routing path for the rehearsal
Customer to run baseline latency/cost comparison vs their on-prem model in staging
Follow-up meeting Wednesday 2026-03-11 to review canary results
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this tight — goal is closure on the fallback postmortem, assign owners, and schedule the sandbox run. We have about an hour.
[00:18] Dr. Lena Moroz: Thanks. Quick note, we had a small bleed of staging traffic to prod during the fingerprint test. It was about 7 minutes — not huge but enough to trigger the safety alarms.
[00:34] Diego Ramos: Right, we reproduced the sequence in staging. Short version: prefix KV cache wasn't warmed, so the runtime routed to the cheaper model variant for latency reasons, but the routing policy didn't correctly map session stickiness, so some sessions got the lower-capability model mid-conversation which caused token expansion and retry loops.
[00:57] Samir Kapoor: Sorry, just to clarify — when you say "cheaper variant" is that the quantized 4-bit model or like a regional fallback?
[01:08] Diego Ramos: Quantized variant, yes — looks like q4_kv_opt, and there was also a cross-region fallback flagged by the smart router when local capacity dropped below threshold. There was a mismatch in the canary route table.
[01:22] Jenna Brooks: And that mismatch caused the bot to repeat? We saw some sessions generate long loops with repeated prompts.
[01:30] Diego Ramos: Exactly, because the model swap mid-KV-cache invalidated the session context effectively. The client retried in a couple of flows which made it exponential for a small subset.
[01:44] Aisha Patel: Important to note — the runtime did not drop data, it was a quality/regression issue, not a data exposure. We double-checked logs and S3 buckets.
[01:55] Tom Hu: Legal here — thanks. Please confirm there was no PII in the leaked logs and the samples you send are sanitized. We'll need that for the audit trail.
[02:05] Diego Ramos: Yep; we'll sanitize. We'll also include request ids and route map snapshots so you can see the routing decision tree.
[02:14] Dr. Lena Moroz: What was the latency impact overall? We saw a small CPU spike in our observability.
[02:21] Maya Li: From our side, p50 was unchanged; p95 increased ~220ms for affected shards during that 7-minute window. Token cost went up ~8% on samples where retries happened.
[02:35] Samir Kapoor: That aligns with what we saw. Cost spike is concerning because we run high volume inference.
[02:42] Aisha Patel: Two levers: fix routing table to enforce model stickiness and introduce a short-lived session lock during model transitions; and warm KV cache more aggressively for newly routed sessions. Diego, do you want to run through the proposed patch?
[02:58] Diego Ramos: Sure — technical, but quick. First, we add a route-evaluation checkpoint during the first 200 tokens to ensure the chosen model variant's KV schema matches the session. Second, if a mismatch is detected, we either wait for KV prefetch (prefetch path) or return a controlled 429 with retry-after header so the client can back off instead of retrying immediately. Third, we add a fallback throttle so cross-region routing doesn't happen unless local is fully saturated.
[03:32] Jenna Brooks: The 429 idea sounds good but how will that affect UX for customers in live traffic?
[03:37] Diego Ramos: It'll be very short — ideal path is 200-500ms extra for a tiny percentage of sessions, which beats uncontrolled retries and cost spikes.
[03:46] Dr. Lena Moroz: Ok, acceptable if it doesn't leak PII and we have a visibility dashboard.
[03:51] Maya Li: We'll add a per-route telemetry dashboard for any 429 events and model-swap events, and we'll surface those in Console and a CSV export.
[04:03] Aisha Patel: Good. Next — sandbox rehearsal. Proposal: Redwood deploys patch to a staging cluster, we run HelioMedix anonymized prompt set across peak 30-min burst and a steady 24-hour profile. Diego will run a 48-hour canary. Samir, can you provide prompt corpus and peak profile?
[04:22] Samir Kapoor: Yes, we'll generate an anonymized set, strip PII, and deliver a CSV and a small replay harness. We aim to have it by Friday.
[04:31] Tom Hu: Legal asks that the replay harness runs in a customer-owned staging VPC with Redwood agent — is that doable?
[04:40] Diego Ramos: Yes, we can run within your VPC for the rehearsal, we have the private control plane for that. We'll need temporary IAM roles and access to the staging S3 bucket for logs.
[04:50] Speaker 2: (inaudible) — role permissions....
[04:54] Aisha Patel: We'll send a checklist for VPC access; Maya will follow up on the SOC/KMS notes.
[04:59] Diego Ramos: Also, small heads-up — during reproduction we saw two rare code paths where a cache eviction triggered while prefetch was in-flight. We have a mitigation that pins prefetch keys for 2 seconds during warm-up. That prevents race.
[05:18] Dr. Lena Moroz: That makes sense. Any chance that pins cause resource bloat?
[05:24] Diego Ramos: Negligible at the 2s timescale; the prefetch pins are scoped by session and auto-evict. We'll monitor.
[05:31] Jenna Brooks: Can Redwood provide a cost delta estimate for leaving pins on permanently versus conditional?
[05:38] Maya Li: We'll run a cost model: conditional pins (only when route switch detected) vs always-on. We'll share a spreadsheet.
[05:46] Samir Kapoor: On the security side, I want confirmation that KMS rotation and audit logs are intact for those routing events.
[05:54] Aisha Patel: Yes — our private deployments use customer-managed KMS if you opt-in; for hosted we use envelope encryption with audit hooks. Maya, can you confirm where those audit logs surface?
[06:06] Maya Li: Console -> Audit -> model-routing. We also push to S3 if requested and can setup a CloudTrail-forward for your SIEM.
[06:14] Tom Hu: We'll request CloudTrail-forward during rehearsal, please include the mapping of IDs to human-readable events.
[06:21] Diego Ramos: Noted.
[06:24] Aisha Patel: Quick risk note — if we hold off the patch there's a small chance it recurs under bursty traffic. We recommend the staging run this week and a limited production canary next week with throttles.
[06:36] Dr. Lena Moroz: Sounds prudent. Timeline?
[06:40] Aisha Patel: Diego will push to staging by 2026-03-09 if we have the prompt set by 2026-03-06. Then 48hr canary ends 2026-03-11, we meet 2026-03-11 to review.
[06:52] Jenna Brooks: Anything for the playbook? We need a clear runbook for on-call in case this surfaces.
[06:58] Maya Li: We'll add a 'fallback loop' appendix to your runbook — steps to identify route-swap by request id, temporary mitigation (throttle route, enable prefetch pins), and escalation path to Redwood SEs.
[07:10] Samir Kapoor: I'll want example queries to grep for and a dashboard link.
[07:15] Diego Ramos: We'll provide both.
[07:18] Aisha Patel: Ok — final check: action item owners and due dates? We have Aisha to share logs (3/6), Samir to deliver corpus (3/6), Diego to deploy to staging and run canary (3/10), Maya to handle SOC/KMS addendum (3/9), Tom to review DPA (3/11). Any objections?
[07:37] Dr. Lena Moroz: None. We appreciate the quick turn.
[07:40] Tom Hu: One more legal note — please include a summary statement in the artefacts stating no data exfiltration occurred; we'll attach that to the compliance record.
[07:51] Diego Ramos: We'll include a signed engineer note as part of the incident package.
[07:56] Aisha Patel: Great. We'll send calendar invites for the rehearsal windows and the March 11 review. Thanks everyone.
[08:05] Jenna Brooks: Thanks.
[08:07] (meeting ends)
